units: <cite ref="Chullin 50b">Ḥull. 50ᵇ</cite> (expl. <he>כרס הפנימי</he>) <he>מן המי׳ ולמטה</he> from where the stomach begins to narrow and downward (the animal being suspended with its head down).

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 109:5">Midr. Till. to CXVIII, 5</cite> <he>מן המ׳ מדבר במצרים</he> ‘out of distress’ (<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 109:5">ib.</cite>) alludes to Egypt; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 875">Yalk. ib. 875</cite>.

senses.gloss: a narrow path marking the boundary between fields, balk, ridge; in gen. boundary.
units: <cite ref="Bava Batra 55a">B. Bath. 55ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="H01494"><he>חֲצָב</he> II</cite>. Y. ib. III, beg. 13ᵈ; Y. Kidd. I, 60ᵈ top <he>אפי׳ מי׳ בנתיים</he> even the (common) balk between them; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 2:1:5">Y. Peah II, beg. 16ᵈ</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 107a:8">B. Mets. 107ᵃ</cite> <he>אילן העומד על המ׳</he> a tree standing on the balk.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 107a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>בממלא כל המ׳ כולו</he> when it covers the entire width of the balk.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 53b:2">B. Bath. 53ᵇ</cite> <he>מי אמרינן האי מ׳ דהאי ארעא ודהאי ארעא הוא</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>מ׳ דארעא חד הוא</he>) do we say, this balk belongs to both fields (and taking possession of it means possession of both)? <cite ref="Bava Batra 53b:3">Ib.</cite> <he>מ׳ אפסרא דארעא וכ׳</he> (Ms. O. <cite ref="M00552"><he>מוֹסֵרָא</he></cite>; differ. in Ms. M.), v. <cite ref="A02766"><he>אַפְסָרָא</he></cite>.
Ib. 62ᵃ מ׳ ראובן וכ׳ the field which I sell thee is contiguous to Reuben’s on the east and on the west side; a. fr.—Pl. מְצָרִים boundary lines, bounds.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 61b:2">Ib. 61ᵇ</cite> <he>אע״פ שמָצַר לו מ׳ החיצונים</he> although he defined (in the agreement) the outermost lines (of the group of buildings or fields), <he>מ׳ הרחיב לו</he> he intended only to give an amplified description of the situation (not to sell him the entire group).

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 7:3">Ib. VII, 3</cite> <he>בסימניו ובמְצָרָיו</he> (if he says, I sell thee a Beth Kor of land) giving its description and boundaries (and it turns out to be less than a Beth Kor); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 118a:8">Sabb. 118ᵃ</cite> <he>נחלה בלא מ׳</he> a boundless possession.
